item.title: Iran using children in security roles in war, reports and witnesses say
item.summary: An 11-year-old is reported to have been killed in an air strike while manning a checkpoint in Tehran.

item.title: Israel says it will keep control over part of southern Lebanon after war with Hezbollah ends
item.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz also says houses in Lebanese villages near the Israeli border will be demolished.

item.title: Peacekeepers killed by roadside explosion in Lebanon, initial report finds
item.summary: The deaths of the two Indonesian nationals came less than a day after another UN peacekeeper - also Indonesian - was killed in Lebanon.

item.title: Judge temporarily halts construction of Trump's White House ballroom
item.summary: The Republican-appointed judge ruled that Trump was a "steward" of the White House, not the owner.

item.title: 'You're no longer my sister' - rows erupt as war divides Iranian families
item.summary: People in Iran describe angry scenes and tense relationships as rifts open up over the war.

item.title: US journalist Shelly Kittleson kidnapped in Baghdad
item.summary: The US state department says a suspect in her abduction has ties to an Iran-backed militia group, Kataib Hezbollah.

item.title: US Army pilots who flew near Kid Rock's home suspended and then reinstated within hours
item.summary: The crews of two military helicopters were suspended by the army, then told there would be "no investigation" by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.

item.title: Wolf bites woman in shock German attack on busy Hamburg shopping street
item.summary: It is believed to be the first wolf attack on a human since the animals began to reestablish themselves in Germany decades ago.

item.title: 'A million things could go wrong' - why seizing Iran's uranium would be so risky for the US
item.summary: Seizing the stockpile would be one of the "most complicated special operations in history", a former defence official tells the BBC.

item.title: India begins counting more than a billion people in massive census
item.summary: The two-phase exercise - the world’s most ambitious - will see three million officials count every Indian.
